To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Participants' level of functioning was an important predictor of the amount of accessibility and attitudinally based barriers they encountered while traveling in China; (2) Participants' income level did not predict the amount of barriers participants experienced; (3) Participants' level and type of mobility assistive device did not predict the level of barriers experienced by participants.

(1) travellers with physical disabilities in China encounter more attitudinal barriers than accessibility barriers; (2) travellers with physical mobility disabilities are more likely to encounter attitudinal barriers and travellers with sensory disabilities are more likely encounter accessibility barriers; and (3) travellers with physical disability are less likely to travel than travellers without disabilities.
(1) the majority of respondents reported encountering accessibility barriers when travelling, and (2) the majority of participants reported encountering attitudinal barriers when travelling.
